clue.text: All but one of the party stand to lose their seats at this

definitions.text: All but one of the party stand to lose their seats at this

parts.words: All but one of the party stand to lose their seats at this
parts.note: reads like a political election wipeout, but describes the children's party game where the music stops and one player each round is left without a chair

explanation.surface: A political party faces an election in which nearly every member will lose a seat in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: In this party game players circle a row of chairs one short of their number, and whoever is left standing when the music stops is out.

clue.text: Moderate idea H. Ford reworked with Model T

indicators.note: something reworked is remade in a new shape, so the letters of the words before and after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Henry Ford refashioned an idea of his together with the Model T car into something unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' shuffles IDEAHFORD and MODELT together; the H. is simply the letter H, and the Model T is Ford's famous car, which makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderate stance avoids extremes, and the middle course between two sides is the idiom for exactly that.

clue.text: Problem on account of tree

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set at school

explanation.surface: Someone faces a difficulty over how a tree has been accounted for.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The sumac is a shrub or small tree whose berries are used as a spice.

clue.text: About to fail with bid?.Almost a disaster

parts.note: a business about to fail is about to close down for good
in bridge a bid is called a call

explanation.surface: A bridge player makes a bid that looks doomed and narrowly escapes ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed text runs the question mark into the next sentence; the definition is the second half. CALL as a bid is bridge jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is a near miss, something that very nearly turned out badly.

clue.text: Accurate volume written by American with a novel ending

parts.note: a litre is a measure of volume, spelt liter in the United States

indicators.note: the ending of the word novel is its final letter

explanation.surface: A book of precise detail written by an American author with a fresh finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written by American' tells you to use the US spelling of the unit; 'ending' takes the last letter of 'novel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A word-for-word, exact rendering is called literal, as in a literal translation.

clue.text: King in Bible said to have great memory

indicators.note: said tells us the letters are spoken, so we write down what the phrase sounds like

parts.note: great is high, and computer memory is RAM, giving high RAM

explanation.surface: A biblical king is reputed to have had a remarkable memory.
explanation.walkthrough: RAM is random-access memory in a computer; 'high RAM' spoken sounds like the king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiram was the king of Tyre in the Old Testament who supplied cedar for Solomon's temple.

clue.text: Fresh out of, initially, vermouth on the rocks

indicators.note: out of here means the first piece lies outside the second, wrapping round it

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky or impudent means insolent

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of the word vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone has run out of vermouth served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' is not 'new' but 'cheeky'; 'out of' puts INSOLENT round V, the first letter of 'vermouth'. 'on the rocks' looks like a drink served over ice but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is in financial ruin, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: In the main, don't offer resistance

definitions.text: In the main, don't offer resistance

parts.words: In the main, don't offer resistance
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this reads as advice to a swimmer not to fight the current, and also as general advice to go along with the majority

explanation.surface: Advice to someone mostly to give way rather than push back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'generally' but is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform with prevailing opinion is pictured as letting the sea's current carry you along.

clue.text: Man and woman getting married

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man and a woman get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the definition: the first man in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the first man created was Adam, and the name is used for man in general.

clue.text: Unconscious king, shot by an archer

parts.note: someone knocked unconscious is out cold
ER, Elizabeth Regina, here stands for a monarch, as R does for king

explanation.surface: A king is struck by an archer's arrow and knocked senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher, standing for the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery a shot landing in the outermost ring of the target, rather than the bull, is called an outer.

clue.text: Become a business executive

definitions.meaning: to look good on, as a colour that becomes you
slang for a person in a business ..., an office manager

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a role as a company boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour that flatters you matches you; and office managers are nicknamed after their formal clothing.

clue.text: Siren making everyone jump

parts.note: everyone means all
to jump a fence is to clear it

explanation.surface: A wailing alarm makes everybody leap with fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siren' is not a temptress but the wartime warning signal that danger has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: In wartime Britain a steady siren sounded after an air raid to signal that the danger was over.

clue.text: Short book about a Caribbean re public

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short book's letters are read backwards

parts.note: Lam is the short form of Lamentations, a book of the Bible
WI, the West Indies, is the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A brief volume concerning one Caribbean republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses LAM to MAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is an African country with an elected president rather than a monarch.

clue.text: Policeman admitting bizarre old laws might be nonsense

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: bizarre signals the letters of the following words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A police officer concedes that some strange old statutes might be absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policeman' suggests a whole word to be defined, but it is the outer piece; the old laws are fodder, not the subject of the nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word means rubbish, foolish talk with no sense in it.

clue.text: Solemn old characters defending church

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
characters means the letters themselves, here used as raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Grave elderly figures stand up for the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' shuffles SOLEMN and O (old) into S + OOLMEN, which surround CH. The whole clue describes the medieval scholastic theologians.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval scholastic philosophers and theologians, who argued for church doctrine, were called by this name.

clue.text: Fellow who's retired hurt is new opener

indicators.note: hurt here means damaged and so altered, signalling the letters around it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket opener has retired hurt and is the newcomer at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired hurt' is a cricket phrase for a batsman who leaves the field injured, but 'hurt' is the anagram signal for IS, N and OPENER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped working and draws a state or company payment is described this way.

clue.text: Snacks as enjoyable as tasty savoury starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters, so each of the next four words gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Snacks that are as delicious as savoury appetisers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' pretends to mean the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, eats are food, especially light bites or snacks.

clue.text: Long letter wanting short answer

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so letters are taken away

parts.note: aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A lengthy letter is sent in reply to a curt answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the letter, but it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn for something is to have an urge for it.

clue.text: Oversleep, say, and be late for public appearance

parts.note: to oversleep is to have a lie-in
to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps late and turns up late for a public engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be late' means to be dead, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead dignitary's body is displayed publicly before burial so mourners can pay respects.

clue.text: Port where Hesperus wrecked? Not right

indicators.note: wrecked suggests broken up, so the letters are rearranged
not means without, so the following letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A port where the ship Hesperus was wrecked, though not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Wreck of the Hesperus' is a Longfellow poem. Drop R from HESPERUS and 'wrecked' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek harbour city on the coast of Asia Minor.

clue.text: Millions one lost in withdrawing capital account

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

indicators.note: lost in means buried inside, so one piece goes within another
withdrawing means drawing back, so the capital's letters are read backwards

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Millions are lost when someone withdraws from a capital account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' reverses ROME to EMOR and 'lost in' puts I inside it. 'capital account' poses as a finance term.
explanation.definitionFit: A written record of one's own life and experiences is an autobiographical account.

clue.text: Rebel without a cause

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to rebel is to rise up

explanation.surface: A rebel with no cause, like the film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebel Without a Cause' is a famous film title; here 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something about, as in to stir up a laugh or a protest.

clue.text: Figure female's about to improve

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a hen is a female bird; the 's is 'is', a link
eight is a figure or number

explanation.surface: A woman is planning to get her figure into better shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' poses as body shape but is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: To intensify or increase something, which is to make it greater.

clue.text: Language rich in dialects, if you look into it

indicators.note: looking into the phrase means finding letters concealed within its words

explanation.surface: A language is full of regional varieties, on closer inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'ricH IN DIalects'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the main official language of India, spoken in many regional varieties.

clue.text: Establish a record

definitions.meaning: British slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: Set down a written account.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up something is to create it; and in British slang someone with previous convictions has this.

clue.text: Writer making money out East with one book

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Far Eastern countries

explanation.surface: An author makes money in the Orient from a single book.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House.

clue.text: Man of the right moving to the left

indicators.note: in an across clue moving to the left means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A man of the political right shifts to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' and 'left' look political; 'right' is a legal entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a man's first name.

clue.text: As China might be, collectively, when in a mess

definitions.meaning: china is crockery, and taken together a full matching set of plates and dishes
a mess is a military dining hall, where the evening meal is brought to the tables

explanation.surface: A country in disarray, considered as a whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' with its capital letter pretends to be the country; 'mess' pretends to be chaos but is a military dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of plates and dishes for a meal is one complete set of crockery.
